title: gpu-instability-postmortem-sketch-2025-02
content:
Quick note: this is a working postmortem + runbook sketch for the cluster-wide GPU instability we observed 2025-02-13 -> 2025-02-14. Draft status: looking for triage/incidence owners from hw-ops and infra.

OVERVIEW:
- Impact: intermittent kernel panics / driver crashes on GPU nodes in prod pool-gpu-1. Roughly 7% of batches experienced mid-request failures; about 3 instances escalated to full node reboots triggered by kernel panic.
- Primary symptoms observed: high rates of ECC correctable errors progressing to uncorrectable ECC on some devices, NVLink link flapping (warnings at driver level), and occasional nvidia.ko oops leading to kernel panic.
- Affected hardware: mixed generation A100 and A10 nodes (rack 3,4).
- Time window: first alert 2025-02-13 03:14 UTC; attenuation started after mitigations at ~2025-02-14 06:40 UTC.

TIMELINE (rough):
- 2025-02-13 03:14 UTC: alert - gpu-ecc-corrected rate spikes (>5000 per hour across pool). Pager to SRE.
- 2025-02-13 03:28 UTC: several pods fail with K8s terminationReason: OOMKilled but kernel logs show 'NVRM: GPU at pci:0000:3d:00: GPU has fallen off the bus'.
- 2025-02-13 03:40 UTC: on-call executed node isolation policy: cordon + drain for top-5 affected nodes.
- 2025-02-13 04:05 UTC: infra noticed NVLink warnings in dmesg on node gpu-rack3-node07: 'NVLINK: Link 1 down, retrying'.
- 2025-02-13 04:40 UTC: one node (gpu-rack4-node02) experienced kernel panic; automatic reboot via IPMI. Post-reboot shows ECC uncorrectable count increment.
- 2025-02-13 07:10 UTC: HW-ops engaged to inspect physical cabling & reseat NVLink bridges on rack 3.
- 2025-02-13 12:00 UTC: patch applied to driver (temp workaround): force-disable nvlink peer-to-peer for A10s, deploy v0.2 of nvidia-utils with stricter health-check and graceful fallback; traffic diverted to dedicated pool-gpu-burst.
- 2025-02-14 06:40 UTC: alert counts returned near baseline; continuous monitoring enabled for 72h.

RAW EVIDENCE (selected extracts):
- dmesg snippet (gpu-rack3-node07):
  [   24.825432] NVRM: GPU 0000:3d:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [   24.825436] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:3d:00 has incurred a PCIe fatal error.
  [   24.825447] kernel: NVRM: The system has reported a non-recoverable error.
  [   24.825460] nvlink: WARNING: Link(1) status changed: DOWN

- nvidia-smi -q output (post-reboot):
  ECC Errors (Volatile)
    Volatile Uncorr. ECC: 12
    Volatile Corr. ECC: 6,432

- kmsg around kernel panic (gpu-rack4-node02):
  ---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
  Call Trace: ... nvidia_ioctl+0x1f4/0x2a0 ...

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION ACTIONS TAKEN (what we did):
- Isolated and drained nodes with fastest rising ECC counts.
- Deployed temporary scheduler taints to prevent new pods scheduling onto exposed GPUs.
- Driver-level mitigation: set NVreg_EnablePCIeGen3=0 for affected nodes (reduced link speed) / forced PCIe retrain; note: this is a temporary knob that reduced flapping but increases latency.
- Steering: steering policy to move best-effort workloads to a separate pool and route latency-sensitive requests to dedicated unaffected capacity.
- Hardware: reseated NVLink bridges and replaced PCIe power connectors on 3 nodes (hw-ops).

INTERIM ANALYSIS (hypotheses):
- Hypothesis A: Progressive hardware degradation on a subset of A100/A10 cards causing rising correctable ECC that eventually yields uncorrectable ECC and NVLink errors. Evidence: persistent increase in correctable counts on same GPU indices.
- Hypothesis B: Driver / kernel interaction regression with our recent nvidia-utils changes + kernel upgrade (5.19.x -> 6.1.8) triggered NVLink negotiation regression under certain thermal/IO conditions. Evidence: rate spikes started shortly after kernel bump in staging and then prod.
- Hypothesis C: Power delivery or PCIe integrity (loose connector / aging riser) causing transient Link Flaps; sealed by reseating. Evidence: HW reseat temporarily reduced one node's error rate.

OPEN QUESTIONS / ACTION ITEMS:
- Long-term: which hypothesis is primary? Need deterministic repro: reproduce on a testbench with identical kernel/driver/firmware combos. Assigned: Priya Raman.
- We need to capture ECC trend data at GPU granularity for 90 days and backfill to compute per-card slope. Assigned: Diego Morales (metrics).
- Should we set alert thresholds to separate 'correctable flood' vs 'uncorrectable present'? Proposed threshold: corrected rate > 2000/hr for > 30m -> page; uncorrectable > 1 -> immediate page.
- Consider adding NVLink link-state to instance diagnostics emitted by node exporter. Assigned: Ethan Park (infra).

RUNBOOK (draft) — On-call quick triage (short checklist to add to SRE runbooks):
1) Symptoms: look at node exporter + cloudwatch: ECC corrected and uncorrected counters; NVLink link state logs in dmesg; kernel oops patterns.
2) Commands to gather context:
   - ssh root@<node> 'dmesg | egrep -i "nvlink|ecc|nvrm|nvidia|GPU has fallen off the bus" -n | tail -n 200'
   - ssh root@<node> 'nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,DRIVER,PWM,FB -x | head -n 200'
   - ssh root@<node> 'journalctl -k -n 300 --no-pager | egrep -i "panic|Oops|NVRM|nvlink"'
   - ssh root@<node> 'cat /sys/class/misc/nvidia0/device/pci_bus(s) 2>/dev/null || true'  # placeholder, check proper sysfs path per driver
3) Minimum mitigation: cordon + drain node; mark taint gpu-instability=true:NoSchedule; reroute traffic.
4) Driver fallback: if NVLink flapping and GPU falls off bus, temporarily set kernel module param to reduce link speed or disable NVLink between problematic pairs (documented as emergency-only).
5) Hardware steps: if errors persist after reboot, schedule immediate HW swap or move cards to test bench. Reseat NVLink bridges only if HW-ops available.
6) Post-action: collect artifacts (dmesg, nvidia-smi -q -x, lspci -vvv, bios/fw versions), upload to S3 with prefix s3://redwood-debug/gpu-incidents/<date>/<node>/ and add JIRA ticket.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS / SUGGESTED PLATFORMS CHANGES:
- Monitoring: split ECC corrected alert and uncorrected alerts; add rate-of-change detector for corrected ECC (slope-alert).
- Observability: include NVLink link state and last driver reset reason in per-node status page. Export via Node Exporter textfile collector.
- Orchestration: implement a temporary 'nvlink-unstable' capability label so control plane can avoid scheduling multi-gpu nvlink-dependent jobs on marginal nodes.
- Automation: automate reseat/swap workflow: if ECC uncorrected observed post-reboot -> create auto-ticket, tag node as hardware-review, and remove from auto-scaler until manual clearance.

SHORT TERM TASK LIST (contributors & ETA):
- Priya: build repro harness on test bench with kernel 6.1.8 + driver X.Y (two weeks).
- Diego: backfill ECC metrics and create slope-based alert (3 days).
- Ethan: exporter telemetry for NVLink link state (4 days).
- HW-ops: inventory NVLink bridge / riser stock & plan preemptive replacements for rack 3/4 (1 week).
- SRE: update runbook with commands + add to on-call rotation notes (2 days).

NOTES TO FUTURE-SELF / ON-CALL HINTS:
- Correctable ECC floods are noisy; don't escalate unless you see uncorrectable or kernel oops. Use slope as a sanity check.
- Reseating NVLink bridges can temporarily mask a failing module; track card IDs and watch for return of errors.
- Watch for correlation with bulk IO or noisy GPU scheduling windows (we saw correlation with nightly retrains).
- When in doubt, preserve artifacts. If node reboots automatically, make sure journalctl --verify/--boot flags capture state.

ATTACHMENTS / REFERENCES:
- Incident ticket: SRE-4821 (linked above)
- Slack thread: #sre-gpu (linked above)
- WIP PR: github.com/redwood-inference/nvidia-utils/pull/78 (driver health-check changes)

END / next steps: please review and add missing owners. I'll schedule a retro for 2025-02-20 to decide long-term remediation (firmware upgrades vs procurement replacements vs software mitigations).

-- Aisha
